poems.note: The headnote identifies these two couplets as an inscription for the coffin of her brother Francis Marrash; they are separately presented from the longer elegy on p. 16.
A separate وقالت heading introduces these five couplets about an evening gathering and an admired companion; a new inscription follows.

The headnote identifies this separately presented two-couplet elegy as mourning a child named Bashir. Its comparison with Gabriel is not treated as evidence of denomination or a devotional classification.
A separate وقالت heading presents three couplets on separation and steadfast affection, before the next headnote.
The book separately presents these two satirical couplets about an unlearned physician between two inscriptions.
The headnote identifies these two couplets as an inscription for a tobacco pouch; they are distinct from the three-couplet pouch inscription earlier on the same page.
The headnote says the two couplets were written on a photograph; the following birth greeting has its own heading.
The headnote identifies a congratulation on the birth of a girl: one couplet on p. 23 continues with two on p. 24. The scan reads ملاك and خط where the unproofread Wikisource page has ملك and فخط.
The headnote presents these two couplets as praise of a barber. The scan and Wikisource read مد كفا; the consulted Qafiyah transcription has مد كفاه.

The headnote presents this two-couplet exchange as suggested by a bereaved woman, not as an established event in the poet's own life. The scan reads شتاتي where the consulted online transcriptions have ستاتي.
